Derivation: exact mean and variance of the bivariate cross nearest-neighbour G function

Source: vignettes/derivation-bivariate.Rmd
derivation-bivariate.Rmd

This vignette proves the closed-form mean and variance of the bivariate cross nearest-neighbour statistic {G_{ij} under a disjoint label-permutation null, again without reference to code. The univariate result of the companion vignette is recovered as the special case {i = j.

1. The null model

The locations {X = \{x_1, \dots, x_N\} are fixed. Two marks (or two phenotypes) {i and {j are present with observed counts {n_i and {n_j, and no location carries both marks. The bivariate CSR null permutes the labels among the locations while preserving those counts, so

{S_i \sim \mathrm{Uniform}\{T \subset X : |T| = n_i\},

and, conditionally on {S_i,

{S_j \sim \mathrm{Uniform}\{T \subset X \setminus S_i : |T| = n_j\}.

This requires {n_i + n_j \le N, which the package checks.

The statistic measures how close type-{i points are to type-{j points,

{G_{ij}(r) \;=\; \frac{1}{n_i} \sum_{p \in S_i} \mathbf{1}\!\left\{ d(p, S_j) \le r \right\}, \qquad d(p, S_j) = \min_{q \in S_j} \|x_p - x_q\|,

with the convention that an empty minimum is {+\infty (so a type-{i point with no type-{j point within {r contributes zero).

2. Indicator decomposition and the conditioning lemma

Put, for each location {p,

{A_p(r) = \{ q \neq p : \|x_p - x_q\| \le r\}, \qquad m_p(r) = |A_p(r)|,

and

{Y_p \;=\; \mathbf{1}\{p \in S_i\} \cdot \mathbf{1}\!\left\{A_p(r) \cap S_j \neq \emptyset\right\}.

Then {G_{ij}(r) = n_i^{-1} \sum_p Y_p. Unlike the univariate case, the indicator involves both random sets.

Lemma 4 (conditional uniformity). Let {T \subseteq X with {|T| = t, and condition on the event {T \subseteq S_i. Then {S_j is uniform over the {n_j-subsets of {X \setminus T. In particular, for any fixed {M \subseteq X \setminus T with {|M| = m,

{\Pr\!\left(S_j \cap M = \emptyset \,\middle|\, T \subseteq S_i\right) \;=\; \frac{\binom{N-t-m}{n_j}}{\binom{N-t}{n_j}} \;=\; T_{N-t,\,n_j}(m).

Proof. The joint law of {(S_i, S_j) is invariant under permutations of {X that preserve the marks, so it can be generated by ordering {X uniformly at random and taking the first {n_i locations as {S_i and the next {n_j as {S_j. Conditional on the set of locations occupying the first {t positions being exactly {T, the remaining {N - t locations are in a uniformly random order, so positions {t+1,\dots,t+n_j form a uniform {n_j-subset of {X\setminus T. Avoidance is then Lemma 1 applied to that ground set. {\square

3. Exact mean

Theorem 3 (bivariate mean).

{\mathbb{E}\big[G_{ij}(r)\big] \;=\; \frac{1}{N} \sum_{p=1}^{N} \Big(1 - T_{N-1,\,n_j}\big(m_p(r)\big)\Big).

Proof. By linearity, {\mathbb{E}[G_{ij}(r)] = n_i^{-1} \sum_p \Pr(Y_p = 1). For fixed {p,

{\Pr(Y_p = 1) = \Pr(p \in S_i)\, \Pr\!\left(A_p(r) \cap S_j = \emptyset\,\middle|\, p \in S_i\right).

Now {\Pr(p\in S_i) = n_i/N, and Lemma 4 with {T = \{p\} (so {t = 1) and {M = A_p(r) \subseteq X\setminus\{p\} gives

{\Pr\!\left(A_p(r) \cap S_j = \emptyset\,\middle|\, p\in S_i\right) = T_{N-1,\,n_j}(m_p).

Multiplying by {n_i/N and dividing the sum by {n_i yields {(1/N)\sum_p (1 - T_{N-1,n_j}(m_p)). {\square

Remark 5 (the mean depends only on {n_j). The type-{i count {n_i enters Theorem 3 only through the prefactor {1/N, so it cancels: the expected cross-{G curve is unchanged if {n_i changes, as long as {n_j, and hence the type-{j mark, is fixed. This asymmetry is intuitive: how many type-{i points there are does not change the chance that a given one finds a type-{j neighbour. It is also visible in the implementation, where only {n_j enters the avoidance table.

4. Exact second moments

Lemma 6 (pair inclusion, bivariate).

{\Pr(p \in S_i,\; q \in S_i) = \frac{n_i(n_i-1)}{N(N-1)} \;=:\; c_2^{(i)},

which is Lemma 2 applied to the uniform {n_i-subset {S_i.

For the joint probability of two hits, define the punctured neighbour sets

{A_p^{\ast} = A_p(r) \setminus \{q\}, \qquad A_q^{\ast} = A_q(r) \setminus \{p\}.

These are the neighbours of {p and {q other than each other, so both are subsets of the ground set {X \setminus \{p,q\} used by Lemma 4 with {T = \{p, q\}, {t = 2. Write

{u_{pq} \;=\; \big| A_p^{\ast} \cup A_q^{\ast} \big| \;=\; m_p^{\ast} + m_q^{\ast} - w_{pq},

where {m_p^{\ast} = |A_p^{\ast}|, {m_q^{\ast}=|A_q^{\ast}| and {w_{pq} = |A_p(r) \cap A_q(r)|.

Lemma 7 (two hits).

{\mathbb{E}[Y_p Y_q] = c_2^{(i)}\, \Big(1 - T_{N-2,\,n_j}(m_p^{\ast}) - T_{N-2,\,n_j}(m_q^{\ast}) + T_{N-2,\,n_j}(u_{pq})\Big).

Proof. {\{Y_p = Y_q = 1\} requires {p, q \in S_i, of probability {c_2^{(i)}, and then that {S_j meets both {A_p(r) and {A_q(r). Conditional on {p,q\in S_i, Lemma 4 with {T = \{p,q\} says {S_j is uniform over the {n_j-subsets of {X \setminus \{p,q\}. On that ground set the relevant neighbour sets are exactly {A_p^{\ast} and {A_q^{\ast}. By inclusion–exclusion,

{\Pr(\text{both met}) = \frac{\binom{N-2-m_p^{\ast}}{n_j}}{\binom{N-2}{n_j}} \!+\! \frac{\binom{N-2-m_q^{\ast}}{n_j}}{\binom{N-2}{n_j}} \!-\! \frac{\binom{N-2-u_{pq}}{n_j}}{\binom{N-2}{n_j}},

which is the stated bracket. {\square

Note that, unlike the univariate case, there is no special short-cut when {\|x_p - x_q\| \le r: the hit condition concerns {S_j, not {S_i. The general formula already covers that situation, because then {q \in A_p(r) so {m_p^{\ast} = m_p - 1, and the corresponding avoidance probability decreases accordingly.

Theorem 4 (bivariate variance).

{\mathrm{Var}\big(G_{ij}(r)\big) \;=\; \frac{1}{n_i^2} \left[\sum_{p=1}^{N} e_p(1 - e_p) + 2\sum_{p<q}\big(f_{pq} - e_p e_q\big)\right],

with {e_p = (n_i/N)(1 - T_{N-1,n_j}(m_p)) and {f_{pq} from Lemma 7.

Proof. Identical to Theorem 2, using the decomposition {G_{ij} = n_i^{-1}\sum_p Y_p. {\square

5. The diagonal case

When the two marks coincide, the natural reading of {G_{ii} is the univariate nearest-neighbour statistic computed on a uniform subset of size {n_i: there is no independent {S_j. The package implements {G_{ii} by delegating to the univariate estimator with {n = n_i, and Theorems 1–2 then apply verbatim. This is the correct reduction because in the univariate problem the neighbour of a marked point may be any other marked point, whereas in Lemma 7 {S_j and {S_i are disjoint.

6. Numerical illustration

For small patterns the bivariate null can be enumerated exhaustively: for each of the {\binom{N}{n_i} choices of {S_i, run over all {\binom{N-n_i}{n_j} choices of {S_j from the remaining locations. With {N = 10, {n_i = 4 and {n_j = 3 this is {\binom{10}{4}\binom{6}{3} = 210 \times 20 = 4200 configurations.

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(permfreeG))
set.seed(11)
N <- 10; ni <- 4; nj <- 3
x <- stats::runif(N); y <- stats::runif(N)
radii <- seq(0, 1.2, by = 0.15)

D <- as.matrix(stats::dist(cbind(x, y)))
ci <- utils::combn(N, ni)
Gsim <- NULL
for (j in seq_len(ncol(ci))) {
  Si <- ci[, j]
  rem <- setdiff(seq_len(N), Si)
  cj <- utils::combn(length(rem), nj)
  for (k in seq_len(ncol(cj))) {
    Sj <- rem[cj[, k]]
    Gsim <- rbind(Gsim,
                  vapply(radii, function(rr)
                    mean(rowSums(D[Si, Sj, drop = FALSE] <= rr) > 0), numeric(1)))
  }
}

d <- data.frame(x = x, y = y,
                m = factor(c(rep("A", ni), rep("B", nj),
                             rep("C", N - ni - nj))))
res <- as.data.frame(exact_gcross(d, radii = radii, mark_col = "m",
                                  marks_i = "A", marks_j = "B"))

c(max_mean_error     = max(abs(res$csr_mean - colMeans(Gsim))),
  max_variance_error = max(abs(res$csr_var -
                               apply(Gsim, 2,
                                     function(z) mean((z - mean(z))^2)))))
#>     max_mean_error max_variance_error 
#>       3.330669e-16       2.359224e-16

Again the errors are pure floating-point round-off.

A direct check of Remark 5 is also immediate: changing {n_i while holding {n_j fixed leaves the exact mean unchanged.

pp <- spatstat.geom::ppp(x, y,
                         window = spatstat.geom::owin(range(x), range(y)),
                         marks = d$m)
a <- permfreeG:::csr_cross_moments_cpp(x, y, radii, 4L, nj)
b <- permfreeG:::csr_cross_moments_cpp(x, y, radii, 5L, nj)
max(abs(a$mean - b$mean))
#> [1] 0
